page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4d server family. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and 62.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. This configuration provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources without overcommitments, as the CPU allocation is fully dedicated.

This instance does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage options. There are zero integrated GPUs on this instance, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or GPU-based machine learning workloads. Additionally, the instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-16 offers a standard resource profile suitable for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces the baseline infrastructure cost, making it a predictable option for general-purpose workloads. Suitable workloads include web serving, application servers, containerized microservices, and moderate database hosting.
